result.topic_en: Latin draft for the Paris prize essay on heat conduction: decomposing the condition F=0 into y-independent equations F_1=0,...,F_m=0 and treating the first case m=1, where by change of variables the differential equation is reduced to a simpler normal form.
result.transcription:
Tribuendo ipsi $y$ valores determinatos diversos
[-(II.)-] ex aequatione (II) inter se x quotientes differen-
tiales ipsius $u$ obtinebantur aequationes diversae,
quarum coëfficientes a $y$ non pendent. Quodsi
ex his aequationibus $m$ sunt a se independentes
$F_1=0,\ F_2=0,\ \dots,\ F_m=0$
ita ut caeterae omnes ex iis sequantur, aequa-
tio $F=0$ necesse est pro quovis ipsius $y$ valore
ex his $m$ aequationibus fluat, unde $F$ for-
mae esse debet:
$c_1F_1+c_2F_2+\dots+c_mF_m$
qua in [-aequatione-] expressione solae quanti-
tates $c$ a $y$ pendent.
Iam casus singulos, quando $m$ est 1, 2, 3, 4
paulo accuratius examinemus simulque ae-
quationes a $y$ independentes, in quas aequatio
$F=0$ dissolvitur, in formas simpliciores re-
digere curemus.
Casus primus, $m=1$.
Si $m=1$, in aequatione II rationes coëffi-
cientium a $y$ non pendebant. At introducen-
do in locum ipsius $y$ novam variabilem $\int u\,dy$
semper effici potest, ut $u$ fiat $=1$, quo pacto
coëfficientes omnes a $y$ evadent independentes.
Porro [-et-] introducendo in locos ipsarum $\alpha,\beta$
novas variabiles semper effici potest, ut $a$ et
$b$ evanescant. Hoc enim eveniet, si expressio
$b\,d\alpha^2-2c'\,d\alpha\,d\beta+a\,d\beta^2$ (quae quadratum ex-
pressionis differentialis linearis esse nequit,
si (2) est forma positiva) in formam
$m\,d\alpha'\,d\beta'$ redigitur et quantitates $\alpha',\beta'$ tanquam
variabiles independentes sumuntur.
Aequatio igitur differentialis (II) hoc in
casu in formam
$2c'\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha\,\partial\beta}+c\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha}+1\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta}=\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$
redigi potest et in forma (2) $a, b$ tunc erunt $=0$
$a'$ et $b'$ functiones lineares ipsius $y$, et $c'$ a $y$
independens. Caeterum patet, temperaturam

methods.what: Since F=0 follows from m independent y-independent equations for every value of y, F must be a linear combination of them whose coefficients alone depend on y
Change of variable y to the integral of u dy, which makes the coefficient u equal to 1 so that all coefficients become independent of y
methods.quote:
introducendo in locum ipsius $y$ novam variabilem $\int u\,dy$
semper effici potest, ut $u$ fiat $=1$

methods.what: Reduce the binary quadratic form to the product form m dα' dβ' (characteristic coordinates) so that a and b vanish
methods.quote:
$b\,d\alpha^2-2c'\,d\alpha\,d\beta+a\,d\beta^2$ (quae quadratum ex-
pressionis differentialis linearis esse nequit,
si (2) est forma positiva) in formam
$m\,d\alpha'\,d\beta'$ redigitur

methods.what: Normal form of the heat equation in the case m=1

items.english: Now let us examine somewhat more carefully the individual cases where m is 1, 2, 3, 4, and at the same time try to bring the y-independent equations into which the equation F=0 decomposes into simpler forms.
